name: field-acoustics
description: Design-time acoustic model for marching drill — what the audience actually hears when the form turns in. Python model plus a TypeScript kernel, held together by a differential suite.
author: USER

data_streams.purpose: Drill coordinate CSVs and optional AES69/SOFA directivity files supplied by the user
data_streams.description: Read on demand from paths the user passes on the command line. Nothing is retained.

notes.ships_no_data: The SOFA loader reads measured directivity but bundles none, and requires a citation rather than accepting one optionally. Measured data whose source nobody can check is not meaningfully better than a fitted curve.
notes.headline_is_assumed: The rear hemisphere rests on an asserted front-to-back array, and turning the form in puts most of the hornline into exactly that region. The provenance report says ASSUMED and so does the product.
notes.dependencies: numpy, scipy and matplotlib — not stdlib-only like the marching-arts core. The TypeScript kernel under kernel/ has no runtime dependencies at all.
notes.licence_trap: TU Berlin's directivity database is CC BY-NC-SA and is deliberately unsupported as a bundled source: the non-commercial clause would propagate to programs that pay for things. BYU's is CC BY 4.0 and is the one to use.
